newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open firmer, boosted by Dow.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open firmer, boosted by Dow.

text.p: Singapore shares were firmer at the open on Thursday boosted by the rebound on Wall Street overnight, said dealers.
"The market is looking a shade better because Wall Street closer higher overnight. Properties and finance stocks seem a bit firmer," said a broker with a local firm.
Index linked stocks like Keppel Corp, Fraser & Neave and Cerebos Pacific were early gainers rising between 10 (US$0.71) and 30 Singapore cents each.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrial index up 9.35 points to 2,229.47 after about 50 minutes of trading.
The UOB-OTC index tracking mostly Malaysian issues was also firmer by 2.40 points to 1,281.22. Total market volume was about 50 million shares with 164 gainers outpacing 28 losers.
Malaysian second-liners continue to dominate the actives list with Arab Malaysian Development and Berjaya Industrial chalking up volume of more than five million shares each.
Leading the gainers was DBS foreign which rose 50 cents to S$19.40. Property heavyweight City Developments also rose 20 cents to S$14.00.
Trading-based Inchcape, Creative and NatSteel shed between 10 and 12 Singapore cents each.
